pinning_lever_exhausted.evidence_already_pinned: the measured 63 GB / 3.05 s = 20.7 GB/s matches the measured pinned bandwidth of 20.0 GB/s
pinning_lever_exhausted.conclusion: the encoder already walks the pinned path, so R202s proposal to switch to pinned has no headroom

table.measured: 3.05-3.14 s, already at the transfer limit

decisive_arithmetic.consequence: as long as every encode_prompt loads 63 GB, about 3.1 s is a hard floor and 2 s cannot be met; this is consistent with compute being only about 0.17 s, i.e. roughly 99 percent of the encoder time is transfer

only_route_residency.if_DiT_fully_resident: 31 GB plus 7.88 equals 38.9 GB, which does not fit
only_route_residency.but: the DiT uses per-block offload, so only a few blocks are resident at once
only_route_residency.condition: the encoder can stay resident if the DiTs steady-state footprint is at most 24.12 GB per rank

converged_question: what is the DiT phases actual steady-state device memory, and is it at most 24.12 GB per rank?

branching.if_yes: encoder residency is feasible, the encoder drops to about 0.5 s and the target is met
branching.if_no: the encoder under-2s target is unreachable unless the transfer method changes, and 20 GB/s is already the link limit; the only alternatives are new hardware or a different dtype, the latter violating keep-original-maths

progression: R201b inferred transfer-bound and flagged it; R202 confirmed the mechanism but its proposed fix was withdrawn in the same round because N=1; R203 gives a hard arithmetic bound and reduces the problem to one measurable number

answer_to_converged_question.question: what is the DiT steady-state device memory, and is it at most 24.12 GB per rank
answer_to_converged_question.answer: already in the receipts: R170 measured the DiT block-interval peak at 7.13 GiB allocated and 11.64 GiB reserved, leaving 20.36 GiB headroom
answer_to_converged_question.condition_met: R203s condition was DiT <= 24.12 GiB per rank; the measured reserved figure of 11.64 GiB satisfies it
answer_to_converged_question.conclusion: encoder residency is memory-feasible with over 13 GiB to spare, so the encoder time becomes pure compute
answer_to_converged_question.math_impact: none - residency changes when weights are loaded, not what is computed

new_real_constraint_host_ram.meaning: the both-resident-on-host, taking-turns-on-device premise needs about 125 GB of usable pinned host memory
new_real_constraint_host_ram.status: MUST BE CHECKED NEXT, and it outranks further projection: if host RAM is insufficient the whole residency route collapses
new_real_constraint_host_ram.how_to_check: free -g on the host plus any pinned-memory limit

status_update: R203 no longer ends on an open question: the memory answer is in the receipts and the route is feasible; the next gate is host RAM
